messages:
Alex K: Heads-up — drafting a short PRD + RFC for kernel selection + attention opt + KV-cache policy changes that we'll aim to land for Q2 runtime release. Link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/ker-opt-kv (WIP). Please skim and drop blockers.

Maria P: Appreciating the prep. Two product asks: 1) ensure low-percentile latency doesn't regress for chat flows, 2) give a config knob for guaranteed regional fallbacks for enterprise customers. Can we include launch criteria for both? :eyes:

Devon L: Will review. Quick thought: kernel selection needs policy-driven heuristics not just static model->kernel mapping. Suggest rules like: seq_len_percentile, batch_size_threshold, hardware_tags -> preferred_kernel. Example snippet:```yaml
kernel_policies:
  - name: short-seq-fp8
    match: {max_seq_p50: 512, batch_p50: 4}
    prefer: fast-attn-fp8
    fallback: generic-fp16
```
Keep it composable.

Sanjay R: Agree on heuristics. For KV cache: customers want predictable mem usage. Propose hybrid eviction: prefix-based pinning + adaptive LRU for rest. Idea: pin prefixes seen in >X% of requests for Y minutes, evict tail by LRU; expose `cache.max_tokens` and `cache.prefix_ttl` in config. Tradeoff: pinning raises mem but reduces repeat work.

Alex K: Good. Maria — can you confirm product acceptance criteria? I'll draft final list.

Maria P: Acceptance criteria (rough):
- 95th/99th p95/p99 token latency not worse than baseline by >10% on chat-heavy sims
- Successful canary: feature on 5 customers for 72h with no errors >1% and no >20ms tail increase
- Config knobs for enterprise (region pin + max_cache_tokens) documented and testable
- Regression tests added to perf-harness and included in CI
- Rollout playbook with automatic fallback to previous kernel on SLA breach

Devon L: For tests, I'll add microbench suites:
- seq_len sweep (16..4096) w/ batch sizes [1,4,16] across kernels
- KV cache hit/miss simulations with long context workloads
- End-to-end chat replay comparing baseline kernel vs new policy (tokens, lat, cost)
I'll mark acceptable thresholds and attach scripts to the RFC.

Sanjay R: Edge cases to call out in RFC:
- model-quantized + fast-attn mismatch -> correctness diffs (need bitwise validation)
- mixed precision fallbacks when kernel unsupported on node -> ensure no OOM
- cross-tenant cache leakage (must namespace caches per-tenant)

Alex K: Nice. Runtime-bot: create RFC checklist item for "kernel selection config schema" and "cache telemetry".
runtime-bot: Created ticket RNW-2741 (RFC checklist + TODOs).

Maria P: Scope negotiation: we can't ship all three pieces in one sweep for Dedicated customers. Prioritize kernel selection + rollout infra for Q2, KV cache policy as opt-in in Q2-beta, attention micro-ops in Q3 unless perf win is >15% on token cost. Agree?

Devon L: Agree with prioritization. Kernel policy + rollout infra give biggest win across workloads. KV cache opt-in path is straightforward to gate.

Sanjay R: For rollout infra, add canary policy: `canary_pct=5, windows=24h, rollback_on: p99_increase>15% or error_rate>1%`. Also capture metrics: token_throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, cache_hit_rate, avg_gpu_mem.

Alex K: I'll update the PRD with those acceptance criteria and the proposed rollout snippet:```yaml
rollout:
  canary_pct: 5
  canary_window_hours: 72
  rollback_conditions:
    - p99_latency_increase_pct: 15
    - error_rate_pct: 1
```

Maria P: Add customer communication plan: pre-notify enterprise customers with Dedicated before enabling kernel auto-routing; provide opt-out TTL and contact for SOC review.

Devon L: I'll add perf dashboards and regression alerts to Console. Also add a synthetic job that runs nightly to detect kernel correctness diffs for a small set of golden prompts.

Sanjay R: One more: add a config `kernel_policy.enforce_mode = [simulate|enforce|audit]` so we can run in simulate for 2 weeks. Simulation should log chosen kernel vs effective kernel and cost delta.

Alex K: Perfect. Next steps: I'll push PRD update by EOD with the acceptance list + rollout YAML + scope notes. Everyone, please leave any last comments inline on the RFC doc. :raised_hands:
